learningObjective: Explain how pipeline parallelism shards a model across devices and what causes pipeline bubbles.

canonicalClaims.claim: PP partitions layers into P contiguous groups, one per device. Single-request forward is sequential across stages, so per-request latency is not reduced; throughput improves via concurrent in-flight requests. Imbalanced stages create bubbles.
conditions: Stages can execute concurrently on different requests.
nonImplications: Does not imply zero bubble in inference.
Does not imply PP is redundant when the model fits on one device.

misconceptions.claim: PP replicates the model on each device.
misconceptions.whyWrong: That is data parallelism; PP shards layers across devices.

misconceptions.claim: PP reduces per-request latency by a factor of P.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Single-request forward is sequential; latency is not reduced (slightly increased).

misconceptions.claim: PP has zero bubble in inference because there is no backward pass.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Imbalanced stage compute and inter-stage transfer still cause bubbles.

implementationFacts: Micro-batching is used to keep stages busy: multiple micro-batches flow through simultaneously.
Inter-stage transfer is a small fraction of stage compute for typical LLM decode.
performanceScenarios: PP is essential when the model exceeds a single device's memory; often combined with TP within a node.
PP scales across nodes better than TP because inter-stage traffic is small (activations per micro-batch).
